hints: Notice that 6 congruent curved sectors form a full circle around the hexagonal arrangement.
walkthrough:
Observe that the 6 identical outer corners of the regular hexagonal packaging sum to a full revolution of $2\pi\text{ rad}$:
$$6\angle PAQ = 2\pi$$

Solve for the angle $\angle PAQ$:
$$\angle PAQ = \frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

ai_rubric.Subtended Angle Proof: Justifies by symmetry/hexagon $6\angle PAQ = 2\pi$ (M1) and establishes $\angle PAQ = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ rad}$ (A1).

hints: Each of the 6 straight rope sections has length $2r = 40\text{ cm}$.
Each of the 6 curved circular arcs has length $r\theta = 20\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$.
Sum all 12 sections to find the total rope length.
walkthrough:
Calculate the length of one straight section of the rope connecting two adjacent outer pipes of radius $r = 20\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Straight length} = 2r = 40\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the length of one curved circular arc around a pipe with $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Arc length} = r\theta = 20\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{20\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

Sum the 6 straight sections and 6 curved arcs:
$$\text{Total rope length} = 6(40) + 6\left(\frac{20\pi}{3}\right) = 240 + 40\pi \approx 365.66 \approx 366\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Rope Length: Finds straight section length $40$ (B1), arc section length $\frac{20\pi}{3}$ (M1), sums $6(40 + \frac{20\pi}{3})$ (DM1), and evaluates to $240 + 40\pi$ (or $366\text{ cm}$) (A1).

hints: Divide the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ into 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length $40\text{ cm}$.
Calculate the total area in exact surd form.
walkthrough:
Divide the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ into 6 equilateral triangles of side length $s = 40\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area of one equilateral triangle} = \frac{1}{2}(40)(40)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 800\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 400\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the total area of hexagon $ABCDEF$:
$$\text{Area of hexagon} = 6 \times 400\sqrt{3} = 2400\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Hexagon Area: Calculates triangle area $400\sqrt{3}$ (B1) and evaluates hexagon area $2400\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$ (B1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: The total region consists of the central hexagon $ABCDEF$, 6 rectangular side regions ($40 \times 20$), and 6 circular corner sectors ($r = 20, \theta = \pi/3$).
walkthrough:
Identify the geometric components composing the total enclosed region:
$$\text{Total Area} = \text{Area of hexagon } ABCDEF + 6 \times \text{Area of rectangle} + 6 \times \text{Area of sector}$$

Calculate the area of the 6 rectangular regions of dimensions $40\text{ cm} \times 20\text{ cm}$:
$$6 \times (40 \times 20) = 6 \times 800 = 4800\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the 6 circular sectors of radius $r = 20\text{ cm}$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ (which combine into one complete circle of radius $20$):
$$6 \times \left[\frac{1}{2}(20^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right] = \pi(20^2) = 400\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Sum the three components to obtain the exact and rounded total area:
$$\text{Total Area} = 2400\sqrt{3} + 4800 + 400\pi \approx 4156.9 + 4800 + 1256.6 = 10\,213.5 \approx 10\,200\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Total Enclosed Area: Calculates rectangle areas $4800$ (B1), sector/circle area $400\pi$ (B1), and sums to $2400\sqrt{3} + 4800 + 400\pi$ (or $10\,200\text{ cm}^2$) (B1).
